Gap Atlas of 505 Global Optimization Instances: GEAR versus Gurobi and SCIP

22 October 2026 · all content is static and readable without JavaScript

Summary. For every instance of the 505-instance benchmark we plot how the certified gap to the best known optimum closes over time and over the number of nodes, for GEAR (final version, one RTX 5090, 421 instances) and for the two strongest baselines in their best configurations, Gurobi and SCIP. Instances are grouped by who certifies them within 180 s: GEAR and at least one of the two baselines (399), GEAR only (22), the baselines only (18), and none of the three (66). Each entry also gives the problem formulation as distributed with the benchmark, the command that runs it, and the complete solver logs.

1. Definitions and data

  • Solvers. GEAR: the final version evaluated in the paper (configuration int3p_crownmerge.yaml), one instance at a time on one RTX 5090 with 16 CPU threads. Gurobi 13.0.3: the best configuration found, which is the default (g0_std: only the gap and feasibility tolerances set to the common standard), 16 threads. SCIP 10.0.2: the best full-benchmark configuration, s2_obbt_pow1 (stronger RLT and OBBT, squared sums not expanded), 16 threads in concurrent mode. All three ran on the same workstation (Ryzen 7 9700X, RTX 5090) with a 180 s wall-clock limit.
  • Certification. A point counts only if it satisfies every original constraint and bound to 10−6 when re-evaluated in the original model, and the solver’s own bounds satisfy P − D ≤ max(10−5, 10−4·max(1, |P|, |D|)). GEAR is scored strictly (replay of its returned point); the baselines use criterion (b) of the released baseline study, which also credits a confirmed infeasibility verdict. GEAR’s total counts its certified infeasibility verdict (mosel_start_folioqpgraph) as the baselines’ criterion does; without it GEAR certifies 420.
  • Reference optimum. P* is the best objective among all points that are feasible to 10−6 and were returned by any of 13 solvers (12 AMPL solvers and GEAR). Maximization problems are negated, so every curve is a minimization gap.
  • Curves. gap(t) = P* − D(t), where D(t) is the best certified lower bound reported by time t (a step function). Values at or below the required gap are drawn on the dashed line; a dot marks a certified instance. The vertical axis is capped at 103·max(1, |P*|) because GEAR’s first CROWN bound can be loose by many orders of magnitude.
  • Axes. Time is wall-clock seconds. For GEAR it is process start-up plus the solver’s cumulative clock; root events are placed at the start and at the end of the lifted-LP phase. Nodes are explored nodes for Gurobi, and lifted-LP nodes plus GPU boxes for GEAR. SCIP’s concurrent mode reports only a final node count, drawn as a single square.
  • Commands. Each entry lists the command that runs that instance for each solver. GEAR’s is the one recorded in its log (#CMD), with <gear> the GEAR source tree, <env> the Python environment, benchmarks the benchmark root and configs the configuration directory. Gurobi and SCIP run one instance through the baseline harness of this repository (baselines/harness/bl.py wave) with the configuration file that produced their logs.
  • Logs. Every entry links to the complete solver logs of the runs shown, with local paths replaced by the placeholders above. The Gurobi logs are the copies in the release archives logs/<solver>.tar.xz of this repository. The Configurations: block at the top of a GEAR log lists the argument defaults, not the settings in effect; those are in the configuration file linked above.
  • Formulations. The AMPL models as released (GAMS-converted scalar form). Variable domains are grouped over consecutive indices; models longer than about 6,000 characters are truncated, and the full file is under the stated path of the released benchmark.

2. Certified by GEAR and by at least one baseline (399)

399 instances: 238 gams_world, 161 minlplib_linear; 287 polynomial or rational, 112 with transcendental functions; median size 6 variables, 3 constraints.
